In Week 7 of STAT 541, we learned about JSON data and using APIs [^1] to predict pass times for the International Space Station (ISS).
This is the first of two collaborative labs during our course. Our team plotted the next 3 predicted pass times
over all US capitals.[^2] I worked with my fellow classmate, Allen Choi. 
We utilized a shared GitHub repository to track changes and make pull requests. We used a moon icon
at each US capital to represent the ISS pass times on a leaflet map.[^3]

Embedded below is the document that Allen and I coded together!


```{=html}
<center>

<iframe src="lab-7.html"
frameborder="1" width="960" height="569" allowfullscreen="true"
mozallowfullscreen="true" webkitallowfullscreen="true"
title="STAT541 Lab 7: Using APIs">
</iframe>

</center>
```



- Our shared GitHub repository for this STAT541 lab is [here](https://github.com/TheAllenChoi/lab-7).

[^1]: Public satellite API (We used the JSON data) from the open-source website: <https://g7vrd.co.uk/public-satellite-pass-rest-api>
[^2]: The longitudes and latitudes of US Capitals are from the [FSU State Capitals Dataset](https://people.sc.fsu.edu/~jburkardt/datasets/states/state_capitals_ll.txt) and [FSU State Names Dataset](https://people.sc.fsu.edu/~jburkardt/datasets/states/state_capitals_name.txt).
[^3]: The icon used in the leaflet map is from [Flaticon](https://www.flaticon.com/free-icons/moon).
